intro: This ながら does not join two actions. ながらに means in the unchanged state of X: something happens while a state stays exactly as it was, from birth, in tears, as in the old days. It attaches to a short list of words, and you can learn them as set phrases.

skills.rule: Set noun or verb stem + ながらに + verb: in that unchanged state; ながらの before a noun.
skills.explain:
The words that take it are few and fixed: 生まれながらに (from birth, by nature), 涙ながらに (in tears), 昔ながらに / 昔ながらの (as it has always been), いながらにして (without leaving where you are), 子供ながらに (young as one was: 子供ながらに感動した) and 陰ながら (quietly, from the sidelines).

The に form modifies a verb: 涙ながらに語った (told it in tears). Before a noun use の: 生まれながらの才能 (an innate talent), 昔ながらの町並み (streets unchanged since the old days). 陰ながら normally appears without に: 陰ながら応援しています. いながらにして adds して and stresses that you did not have to move: 家にいながらにして世界中の映画が見られる. There is no ながらで.

The edge: 食べながら is two actions at the same moment, with any action verb. ながらも is although (狭いながらも楽しい家). If you can translate as still in the state of, as it always was, or from birth, it is ながらに.
patterns: 生まれ / 涙 / 昔 ながらに [verb]
生まれ / 昔 ながらの [noun]
[place] に いながらにして [potential verb]
陰ながら [応援する / 祈る]

examples.jp: 母[はは]は涙[なみだ]{ながらに}事故[じこ]のことを話[はな]した。
examples.en: My mother talked about the accident in tears.

examples.jp: この町[まち]には昔[むかし]{ながらの}町並[まちな]みが残[のこ]っている。
examples.en: This town still has streets that look the way they always have.

examples.jp: 陰[かげ]{ながら}応援[おうえん]しています。
あの選手[せんしゅ]には生[う]まれ{ながらの}才能[さいのう]がある。
examples.en: That player has a natural-born talent.

examples.jp: 人[ひと]は生[う]まれ{ながらに}して平等[びょうどう]である。
今[いま]は家[いえ]にい{ながらにして}、世界中[せかいじゅう]の映画[えいが]が見[み]られる。
examples.en: Now you can watch films from all over the world without leaving home.

contrast.note: 音楽を聞きながら勉強する: two actions at once, with any verb. ながらに takes only the set words and describes a state, not a second action.
狭いながらも, 知りつつ: although. 涙ながらに is never although; it is in tears.
がてら and かたわら combine two activities (散歩がてら, 仕事のかたわら). ながらに never introduces a second activity.

mistakes.bad: 音楽[おんがく]を聞[き]き{ながらに}勉強[べんきょう]する。
mistakes.good: 音楽[おんがく]を聞[き]き{ながら}勉強[べんきょう]する。
mistakes.note: Two simultaneous actions take plain ながら. ながらに is only for set states such as 涙ながらに.

mistakes.bad: 狭[せま]い{ながらに}楽[たの]しい家[いえ]です。
mistakes.good: 狭[せま]い{ながらも}楽[たの]しい家[いえ]です。
mistakes.note: Although after an adjective is ながらも. ながらに is limited to its set words (涙, 生まれ, 昔, 子供) and is not a general although.

mistakes.bad: 涙[なみだ]{ながらで}謝[あやま]った。
mistakes.good: 涙[なみだ]{ながらに}謝[あやま]った。
mistakes.note: The adverb form is ながらに and the noun-modifying form is ながらの. There is no ながらで.

skills.tip: Is it from birth, in tears or as in the old days, with no second action going on? ながらに. Two actions at once is plain ながら.
